title: Reversible Svelte 5 catalogue shell

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
Approved rationale, preservation boundary, visual checkpoint, promotion criteria, cadence, stops, and deferrals for the reversible Svelte catalogue-shell proof.
Accepted product sequence places the Svelte shell gate after certified rank 5 and before rank 6.

allowedWork: Integrate pinned Svelte 5 and its Vite plugin behind an isolated catalogue entry; extract typed framework-neutral host joints; reproduce the approved catalogue shell; add focused browser, visual, architecture, and performance proof; promote only after the vector checkpoint.
Preserve the current imperative catalogue route as the rollback path until the approved visual checkpoint; commit every verified slice independently.
disallowedWork: Do not move animation assets, semantic truth, runtime frames, clocks, renderer ports, authoring commands, or publication bundles into Svelte.
Do not implement SvelteKit, Internal Studio, Public Web, rank 6, LLM work, a motif registry, or catalogue-wide redesign in this contract.
Do not execute s17 through s26 until the user explicitly approves the s16 visual exemplar.
goal: Replace only the catalogue's imperative application composition with a reversible Svelte 5 shell while preserving framework-neutral animation authority, route and Review lifecycles, selected capability loading, static truth, accessibility, and production budgets.
commitCadence: Commit after each independently verified slice.
stopConditions: Stop at s16 for explicit human visual approval before route promotion or caller generalization.
Stop if work would create a second loader, clock, Review history, URL authority, renderer path, or semantic state.
Stop if a selected capability enters the default startup path or an existing performance or bundle ceiling would need widening.
Stop if visual parity requires an unapproved redesign, compatibility requires changing canonical public behavior, or durable verification is missing or contradictory.

slices.title: Freeze catalogue baseline and budgets
slices.summary: Frozen the current catalogue DOM and lifecycle ownership, visual exemplar, production bundle ceilings and measurements, runtime targets and observations, plus the pre-existing KaTeX attribution discrepancy. Added a stable 14-check migration baseline command.

slices.title: Integrate pinned Svelte 5 tooling without route cutover
slices.summary: Integrated exact Svelte 5.56.8, Vite plugin 7.2.0, and svelte-check 4.7.4 in runes mode. Added an isolated compiler canary and stable typecheck; the imperative bootstrap, production route graph, and bundle measurements remain unchanged.

slices.title: Extract framework-neutral catalogue host view model
slices.summary: Extracted one framework-neutral selected catalogue view model, pure chrome reducer, and typed host command boundary. The active imperative shell consumes it while loaders, clocks, URL, Review, renderers, and generated-session internals retain their prior authorities.

slices.title: Extract asset preparation and capability host services
slices.summary: Centralized both catalogue hosts on one explicit-search selection preparation service and one shared four-module lazy capability host. Removed duplicate preparation methods and promise fields while leaving asset caching, runtime clocks, renderer registration, and URL authority in their existing owners.

slices.title: Mount isolated Svelte exemplar entry
slices.summary: Mounted a migration-only Svelte 5 exemplar through one dynamic bootstrap branch. It consumes the shared preparation service and selected-host view model; canonical catalogue requests continue using the independently tested imperative rollback host without requesting the Svelte entry.

slices.title: Reproduce outer shell and terminal states
slices.summary: Reproduced the canonical three-region catalogue frame and its loading, not-found, error, and selected states in Svelte using existing CSS and stage reservation. Search behavior, player hydration, inspector controls, navigation, and Review remain explicitly deferred to later slices.

slices.title: Port fuzzy search and stable selection
slices.summary: Ported reactive fuzzy search through one shared framework-neutral result-row projection consumed by both hosts. Filtering changes only the rail projection; selected artifact identity, stage content, health authority, and URL remain stable.

slices.title: Mount existing player controller in Svelte stage
slices.summary: Mounted the existing player shell, surface registry, playback controller, and paint-observation lifecycle through one shared browser host consumed by Svelte and imperative catalogue shells. The vector graph paints and scrubs on the original clock, and rail search preserves the same player node.

slices.title: Port inspector and tuning controls
slices.summary: Mounted the canonical Details, Parameters, Tuning, and optional explanation inspector projection in Svelte. Both hosts share one inspector-control adapter; presentation tuning commands the existing player capability and panel changes preserve the inspector DOM.

slices.title: Port cancellable in-shell asset switching
slices.summary: Ported in-shell selection through the existing projection and one shared preparation service. A monotonic revision guard ignores stale pack completions, while the three-region shell remains mounted and only the selected player lifecycle is replaced.

slices.title: Port URL history and playhead restoration
slices.summary: Ported artifact history push, frame-driven playhead replacement, and Back/Forward restoration through the existing route codec and navigation decisions. The Svelte host opt-in remains separate metadata and all history selection reuses the cancellable preparation path.

slices.title: Preserve focus keyboard and rail scroll behavior
slices.summary: Consolidated overlay keyboard behavior, focus snapshots and restoration, and rail scroll preservation into one interaction host used by both catalogue shells. Corrected scroll ownership to the actual result-list viewport and browser-verified selection and narrow Escape behavior.

slices.title: Preserve Review composer and draft lifecycle
slices.summary: Centralized both catalogue shells on one idempotent development Review host. It dynamically mounts the existing provider once, preserves the same composer and draft across selection and history changes, and disposes once with the owning application.
